filter: In a network that looks at pictures: a small grid of weights that is slid across the picture to detect one pattern, such as an edge. Also called a kernel.
kernel: Another name for a filter: the small grid of weights a convolutional layer slides across a picture.
convolution: Sliding a small filter across a picture and, at every stop, multiplying the pixels under it by the filter’s weights and adding them up.
feature map: The grid of numbers a filter produces: big where its pattern was found in the picture, near zero where it was not.
weight sharing: Using the same weights at every position of a picture, so a pattern learned in one place is recognized everywhere.
convolutional layer: A layer made of several filters. Each one slides over the same input and produces its own feature map.
convolutional network: A network built from layers of filters that slide across a picture, usually with pooling in between. Often shortened to CNN.
pooling: Shrinking a feature map by replacing each small block of numbers with a single number.
max pooling: Pooling that keeps only the biggest number in each block.
padding: In a convolutional network: a border of zeros added around a picture so the feature map comes out the same size as the picture.
data augmentation: Training on deliberately altered copies of the examples, such as shifted or rotated pictures, so the network learns to ignore those changes.
